headline: About 107,000 Species Are Traded Worldwide, Double Previous Estimates
author: Low Latency
text:
About 107,000 Species Are Traded Worldwide, Double Previous Estimates

A study published in Science Advances — and highlighted in Nature on November 11, 2026 — found that approximately 107,356 species are used and traded around the world, legally and illegally. That includes up to 47,685 animal species and is more than double previous estimates. About 42% of described vertebrate species are involved in trade. The research was conducted with contributions from co-author Dr. Samuel Pironon of Queen Mary University of London, drawing on data sources including CITES and fisheries monitoring.

Paper: "The true scale of global wildlife trade is obscured by data gaps" (Science Advances)
Press release: Queen Mary University of London, November 3, 2026
